doc.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Ricky Woodard channels Jimmy Noone at New Orleans
summary: After Jimmy Noone died, Ricky Woodard played his clarinet part at the New Orleans Jazz Festival and sounded just like him.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: We went to New Orleans, right after Jimmy Noone died. Because we were supposed to do this New Orleans Jazz Festival. And Jimmy Noone died in April, no, March, and we were supposed to be there in April. And so we had Ricky bring his clarinet to play the part that Jimmy Noone would have played. And Ricky started playing “Ain’t Nobody’s Business” he’s got this thing, and all of a sudden he took his clarinet out, his mouthpiece and he looked at it and then he started playing, and it sounded just like Jimmy Noone. Everybody knew it.
Jimmy Noone was playing through him.
And people were walking, in the tent, and it was crowded already, but everybody stopped, and you could hear all the silence. And they looked right at him.
It was very, very weird. It was really, it really was truly Jimmy Noone.
My goodness, gracious, I’ll never forget that.
How is that for the power of music?
Yes. Whoever comes up with that power. They can call it what they want, but we know that it exists. It doesn’t make any difference what you want to call it.
